Fragments of marginal text at the left edge of the column, cut off and largely unreadable. Cropped strip of text at the right edge of the scan, probably from the neighbouring page.

main_text.p: pauciores quàm sexies mille, ut suffragium ferentes ætate minores non essent quàm annis lx. Merces his judicibus statuta oboli tres, id est, media drachma. Hoc judicio quondam ex urbe exterminatus fuit Aristides ob invidiosum nomen Justi; ejectus è patriâ Themistocles ob immodicam gloriam.

head.i: Ratio conficienda subitò pecunia in usum reipublica poscente aliquâ necessitate.

main_text.p: [illegible, ~6 letters]Aliud etiam institutum post tempora Solonis in civitatem introductum, usu compertum valdè salutare, sed sensim sub initia Philippi Macedonis, & oratoris Demosthenis, oratorum turbidorum vitio degenerans. Cujus scopus ab initio erat, ingruente aliquâ ab hoste necessitate, subitò in usum parandæ classis & aliorum belli onerum pecuniam necessariam conficere. In hunc finem ex quâlibet tribu, quæ decem erant, deligebant ditiores cives cxx, qui pro republicâ munera obirent: Et hi vilissimi se dividebant in partes binas pares civium sexagenûm numero, sed opibus impares. Nam qui opulentissimi [?]abebantur in partem priorem, qui minus opulenti in posteriorem referebantur: dicebaturque quælibet harum partium

page.notes: Page number and running head read from the top of the page. The left margin has fragments of printed text (for example beside "ab initio" and the lines below "paranda"), but they are too cut off to read; the one note shown is a placeholder for them and its position is approximate. The right edge of the scan carries a strip of cut-off text that I could not read and did not transcribe. "abebantur" is probably "habebantur" with the h lost in print; I have marked it [?] and left the printed form. The second half of the last line ("tium") is the end of a word broken at the line end, so the paragraph is complete as printed on this page. No catchword or signature is visible.
